userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC as part of two larger accessions in 2021. These accessions were ingested by the RAC as Accessions 2021:067 and 2021:108.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is comprised of one series. Original order was maintained as much as possible.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection contains the office files of the Ford Foundation's Middle East and North Africa Regional Office, based in Cairo, Egypt. The contents of the collection reflect how the structure and program interests of the Foundation's Middle East and North Africa programming have changed over the years as well as how the relationship between the specific Cairo Office and the larger regional program have evolved.

The collection includes materials that date back to the early history of the Cairo Office in the late 1950s when the Office managed programming for Egypt (which was, at that time, the United Arab Republic) and was under the umbrella of the Foundation's Middle East (formerly Near East) program, headquartered at the Beirut, Lebanon Office. Documents in the collection carry through into the mid-1970s when the Foundation transferred its regional Middle East headquarters to the Cairo Office because of the Lebanese Civil War. The collection includes files created by the Beirut Office that help document the Foundation's broader Middle East regional programming that the Cairo Office took over.

Materials in the collection document a larger span of the Cairo Office's history with inclusion of materials dating up to the early 1990s. These materials show the Cairo Office's expansion to the Middle East and North Africa Office. The Foundation's North Africa program had formerly been based in the Tunis, Tunisia Office until that office closed in 1978. Between the 1970s and 1990s, the Cairo Office also operated a sub-office in Khartoum, Sudan.

Because of the broadening regional responsibility of the Cairo Office, the collection holds materials documenting the Foundation's programming in Egypt (officially, the Arab Republic of Egypt) as well as a number of other countries in the Middle East and North Africa region, including Lebanon, Sudan, Syria, Jordan, Palestine, Tunisia, Iran, Yemen, and the Arab Gulf States, particularly Saudi Arabia.

The collection is comprised of one series of subject files created between the 1950s and the early 1990s. In Egypt and other countries in the Middle East and North Africa, the Ford Foundation provided grant support in a number of fields including:
- Economic development and regional planning
- Public administration
- Management training and workforce development
- Agriculture, food, irrigation and water resources, rural development, and environment and natural resources management
- Education
- English language training
- Reproductive health, population, maternal health, child survival, and family planning
- Women's centered programming such as in rights, economic development, and health
- Refugee assistance
- Human rights
Material formats found within the collection include correspondence, reports, memos, grant records, proposals, meeting materials, articles, press clips, and a few photographs.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation has operated an office in Cairo, Egypt since the late 1950s, and over the course of the Cairo Office's lifespan, it has transformed to become the headquarters of the Foundation's programming for the Middle East and North Africa region.

Changes in the Cairo Office's structure throughout its history parallel changes in the country of Egypt (officially, the Arab Republic of Egypt) itself because when the Cairo Office first opened, Egypt was the United Arab Republic. The Cairo Office was originally part of the Foundation's Middle East (formerly Near East) program, headquartered at its Beirut Lebanon, Office. At different points throughout its history the Middle East program had, in addition to its presence in Egypt and Lebanon, offices and program representatives in Turkey, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Bahrain. A separate North Africa program was operated out of the Foundation's office in Tunis, Tunisia.

At the time of the Lebanese Civil War in the mid-1970s, the Ford Foundation transferred its Middle East program headquarters to its Cairo Office. For the most part, the Middle East program was consolidated to just the Cairo Office during this time. The Foundation also closed its Tunis Office a short while later in 1978, and the Cairo Office expanded to manage the Foundation's Middle East and North Africa regional program. Between the 1970s and 1996, the Cairo Office also operated a sub-office in Khartoum, Sudan.

Throughout its history, the Cairo Office and the larger Ford Foundation Middle East and North Africa regional program have managed grants in economic development, public administration, agriculture, education, family planning, reproductive health and rights, and women's rights. In addition to programming for Egypt, the Cairo Office has also managed programming in Syria, Yemen, Jordan, Palestine, Lebanon, Sudan, the Arab Gulf States, and other countries in the Middle East and North Africa.

Representatives based in the Cairo Office have included Guillame de Spoelberch, John D. Gerhart, S. Lee Travers, David Nygaard, Humphrey Davies, Steven Lawry, Omotade Aina, and Emma Playfair, among others.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series contains the subject files of the Ford Foundation's Middle East and North Africa Regional Office in Cairo, Egypt. Subject files primarily relate to the program activities of the Cairo Office from between the late 1950s through the early 1990s. If additional records are added to the series, they may perhaps document more recent history of the Office.

The subject files provide insight into the Cairo Office's programming for Egypt (officially, the Arab Republic of Egypt) which, at the time of the Office's establishment and for several years of its early history, was the United Arab Republic. The files also document the Cairo Office's evolving responsibility for the Ford Foundation's programming for the Middle East and North Africa region. Records in the series that were created around the mid-1970s show the transfer of the Ford Foundation's regional headquarters for its Middle East programming to the Cairo Office. Prior to that transfer, the headquarters had been at the Foundation's Beirut, Lebanon Office. Some of the materials created by the Beirut Office for the Middle East program are included in the series. Later files in the series show the Cairo Office's absorption of the Foundation's programming for North Africa after the closure of the North Africa program's former headquarters in Tunis, Tunisia in 1978.

Earlier files in the series document the Cairo Office's collaboration with other Ford Foundation offices and representatives in the Middle East and North Africa countries of Lebanon, Saudia Arabia, Jordan, and Tunisia. As the consolidated Office for the Middle East and North Africa, the Cairo Office collaborated with the Foundation's other regional African Office like its Office for East Africa in Nairobi, Kenya. There are also files documenting the Cairo Office working with a sub-office it operated in Khartoum, Sudan between the 1970s and 1990s.
Various organizational schemes have been used to organize the files. Some files are organized under organization name, others by country, and others by topic.
A significant portion of the files in the series concern the Cairo Office's women's programs. Much of this work was organized by Program Officers Cynthia Myntti and Barbara Ibrahim.
